DEC_AGENT_BY_HAND.alternatives: start the agent automatically when a review is finished.
DEC_AGENT_BY_HAND.reason: monsterbrain offers (button, key), the user decides; no event – e.g. a finished review – starts an agent.
DEC_AGENT_BY_HAND.title: Agent actions are only ever started by hand

DEC_AGENT_GENERIC.alternatives: the action built into monsterbrain; deciwa storing when the agent was last informed.
DEC_AGENT_GENERIC.reason: monsterbrain knows sessions and concepts, deciwa knows the review; every review entry has a created time, so Claude finds what is new itself and deciwa keeps no per-user files.
DEC_AGENT_GENERIC.title: Generic parts in monsterbrain, the review action in deciwa, no extra review state

DEC_AGENT_RUNNING_SESSION.alternatives: a new background session per action, MCP prompts as slash commands, copying the prompt.
DEC_AGENT_RUNNING_SESSION.reason: You and Claude work on the result together, with the chat context of the session.
DEC_AGENT_RUNNING_SESSION.title: Agent actions go to the running Claude Code session

DEC_AGENT_SOCKET.alternatives: channels only (terminal); a deep link per action (prefilled only, a new session each time); an MCP tool Claude would have to poll.
DEC_AGENT_SOCKET.reason: Works in the Claude desktop app, where channels are not available, and needs no start script or flag. The interface is undocumented; that risk is accepted, the dialog is the fallback.
DEC_AGENT_SOCKET.title: Agent actions go through the session's messaging socket

DEC_CHANGES_ON_FOLDERS.reason: The knowledge folder and the code repositories next to it are watched the same way.
DEC_CHANGES_ON_FOLDERS.title: The change view works on folders; Git supplies changes where a folder is a repository

DEC_CLAUDE_ACTIONS_IN_APP.reason: Concepts and free messages are not review; they work without deciwa. deciwa adds what it knows – the review of concept.md – through ctx.agentPrompt.
DEC_CLAUDE_ACTIONS_IN_APP.title: Concept actions and the message live in monsterbrain; extensions add to their prompts

DEC_CLAUDE_BUTTON.alternatives: one button that always opens the menu; a button per action.
DEC_CLAUDE_BUTTON.reason: The frequent action (an extension's main entry, deciwa: Inform Claude) stays one click; everything else is one menu away.
DEC_CLAUDE_BUTTON.title: One Claude button per file: a split button with a menu

DEC_CLAUDE_MCP.alternatives: a chat panel inside the app (embedded terminal or Agent SDK).
DEC_CLAUDE_MCP.reason: The most for the least effort, one chat place, works with every MCP-capable agent, no API key in the app.
DEC_CLAUDE_MCP.title: Claude controls the app through a local MCP server; a chat inside the app comes later

DEC_CLOSE_IS_APPROVAL.alternatives: the entry only enabled when the status is approved.
DEC_CLOSE_IS_APPROVAL.reason: One click instead of editing the status first; monsterbrain asks before it goes out.
DEC_CLOSE_IS_APPROVAL.title: "Close concept" is the approval

DEC_CONCEPT_ACTIONS_INSIDE.alternatives: concept actions for every file a concept lists.
DEC_CONCEPT_ACTIONS_INSIDE.reason: A fact or an output a concept lists under results: is not the concept; implementing or closing it from there surprises.
DEC_CONCEPT_ACTIONS_INSIDE.title: Concept actions only for files inside the concept's folder

DEC_DESKTOP_APP.alternatives: a local server opened in the browser.
DEC_DESKTOP_APP.reason: The app starts, watches and stops whatever it needs internally; no console.
DEC_DESKTOP_APP.title: A desktop app, not a server started by hand

DEC_DISCARDED_EVERYWHERE.alternatives: dropped for backlog items, discarded for concepts.
DEC_DISCARDED_EVERYWHERE.reason: Concepts and backlog items are abandoned the same way; one status and one menu word (Discard) for both. A discarded concept stays in its folder, a discarded backlog item moves to the archive like a done one.
DEC_DISCARDED_EVERYWHERE.title: One word for "not wanted any more": discarded, for concepts and backlog items

DEC_DISCARD_STATUS_ONLY.alternatives: archive the folder with a skill; delete it.
DEC_DISCARD_STATUS_ONLY.reason: Nothing is lost and nothing needs Claude; a discarded concept counts as closed.
DEC_DISCARD_STATUS_ONLY.title: "Discard concept" only sets status: discarded

DEC_ELECTRON.alternatives: Tauri – much smaller download and RAM, but a different web engine per OS (WebKitGTK on Linux) and Rust as a second language.
DEC_ELECTRON.reason: The same Chromium on every system, so HTML outputs look like in Chrome; Linux is stable; one language for UI and core.
DEC_ELECTRON.title: Electron with TypeScript

DEC_IMAGE_CLICK.alternatives: a lightbox over the file; zoom inside the rendered Markdown.
DEC_IMAGE_CLICK.reason: A picture in a concept is often too small to read; on its own it can be zoomed. In deciwa's review mode a plain click stays with the review, Ctrl click opens – as for links. Pictures in HTML pages stay out.
DEC_IMAGE_CLICK.title: A click on a picture opens it as its own file

DEC_IMAGE_ZOOM_KEYS.alternatives: 0 for fit and 1 for 1:1, a double click to toggle.
DEC_IMAGE_ZOOM_KEYS.reason: deciwa uses digits for stars and letters for its review; Fit and 1:1 are buttons, zoom also works with Ctrl and the wheel or a pinch.
DEC_IMAGE_ZOOM_KEYS.title: The image view zooms with + and - only, no other single keys

DEC_IMPLEMENT_ALL_TASKS.alternatives: only the next task per click.
DEC_IMPLEMENT_ALL_TASKS.reason: The task list is the plan; ideas and notes elsewhere in the concept are not work yet. A task that needs the user ends the run; tasks rejected in deciwa are skipped.
DEC_IMPLEMENT_ALL_TASKS.title: "Implement concept" does every open task of ## Tasks, and nothing else

DEC_LAYOUT.reason: As in the viewer mockup, with the danwos tool branding.
DEC_LAYOUT.title: Layout: tree left, content in the middle, metadata right

DEC_MESSAGE_NEEDS_FILE.alternatives: a message about the whole folder.
DEC_MESSAGE_NEEDS_FILE.reason: The open file is the context of the message.
DEC_MESSAGE_NEEDS_FILE.title: "Message to Claude" only with an open file

DEC_NO_INTERACTION_STATE.alternatives: an own "seen" state in the app.
DEC_NO_INTERACTION_STATE.reason: Seen, read and done are review state – a deciwa feature that comes with the deciwa extension.
DEC_NO_INTERACTION_STATE.title: monsterbrain keeps no state about user interactions

DEC_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.alternatives: the idle session first (actions landed in the wrong session); always ask; a session claims a concept through an MCP tool.
DEC_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.reason: Several sessions often work in the same folder, one per concept; the one that did the concept's work has its context. A busy session may get it; with none, Daniel picks.
DEC_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.title: The session that works on the concept gets the action

DEC_START_CLAUDE_HERE.alternatives: a setup button with a short command, an embedded terminal in the app, a Claude Code plugin.
DEC_START_CLAUDE_HERE.reason: One click when no session listens; the start script and the channel flag stay hidden. Since 2026-10-30 the dialog offers a new desktop session first and the terminal second (DEC_AGENT_SOCKET).
DEC_START_CLAUDE_HERE.title: "Start Claude here" is enough to make agent actions simple

DEC_STRUCTURE_UNCHANGED.reason: The folder belongs to its user and their agents; the app adapts to it.
DEC_STRUCTURE_UNCHANGED.title: The folder structure stays unchanged – monsterbrain reads it and imposes none

DEC_TAB_HISTORY.alternatives: one history for the whole window; the tree's files in the history too.
DEC_TAB_HISTORY.reason: After following a picture or link far away in the tree, one click on the mouse's back button returns to the same view and scroll position. Files opened from the tree or with j / k replace the preview tab and stay out – the tree is a quick look.
DEC_TAB_HISTORY.title: Back and forward per tab, like a browser, only through link and picture clicks

DEC_TASK_ACTIONS.alternatives: every backlog task goes through a concept.
DEC_TASK_ACTIONS.reason: A small task can be done without a concept. Claude asks first when the task is unclear and does not close it itself; closing or discarding is a click of the user.
DEC_TASK_ACTIONS.title: Backlog tasks get their own Claude actions: implement, close and discard

DEC_TWO_REPOS.reason: The setup (folder skeleton, AGENTS.md, templates, skills, example section) is shared on its own; the app is distributed later.
DEC_TWO_REPOS.title: Two repositories: the app, and later the shareable brain setup

PROP_AGENT_SOCKET.alternatives: channels only (terminal); a deep link per action (prefilled only, a new session each time); an MCP tool Claude would have to poll.
PROP_AGENT_SOCKET.reason: Works in the desktop app, where channels are not available, and needs no start script or flag. Tested with Claude Code 2.1.309 on Linux.
PROP_AGENT_SOCKET.section_name: Agent actions through the session’s socket
sections: Agent actions through the session’s socket
PROP_AGENT_SOCKET.title: Agent actions go through the session's messaging socket

PROP_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.alternatives: the idle session first (the first prototype – actions landed in the wrong session); always ask; a session claims a concept through an MCP tool.
PROP_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.reason: Several sessions often work in the same folder, one per concept; the one that did the concept's work has its context.
PROP_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.section_name: Agent actions through the session’s socket
sections: Agent actions through the session’s socket
PROP_SESSION_BY_CONCEPT.title: The session that works on the concept gets the action

Q_ACTIONS_AS_FILES.title: Agent actions as files in the knowledge folder (one Markdown file per action, frontmatter = fields, body = prompt) – wanted, and part of the shareable brain setup?

Q_CHANGE_FOLDERS.title: Which folders besides the open one belong in the change view, and where is that list kept – in the app settings or in a file in the folder?

Q_CHANNEL_DESKTOP.title: Do Claude Code channels reach a session in the Code tab of the Claude desktop app, or only the CLI?

Q_CLOSE_VIA_SOCKET.title: "Close concept" is the approval, but a socket message counts as another session's request, which cannot approve anything – enough that monsterbrain asks first and Claude may ask once more, or should Close concept go through the prefilled deep link that you send yourself?

Q_FRONTMATTER_DIFF.title: Changed frontmatter is not visible in the rendered diff – show the changed keys in the right panel?

Q_IGNORED_FILES.title: Files ignored by Git (build folders, personal raw data) – show, dim or hide them in the tree?

Q_NON_GIT_FOLDERS.title: Folders that are not Git repositories – show changes by modification date only, or leave them out?

Q_SOCKET_UNDOCUMENTED.title: The session registry and the message line are undocumented and may change with a Claude Code update – accept that, with the dialog as fallback?

alternatives.description: options that were considered and not taken

arch.description: Mapping of uml key to uml content.

constraints.description: List of constraint names, which are defined for this need.

constraints_error.description: An error message set if any constraint failed, and `error_message` field is set in config.

constraints_passed.description: True if all constraints passed, False if any failed, None if not yet checked.

constraints_results.description: Mapping of constraint name, to check name, to result, None if not yet checked.

content.description: The main content of the need.

docname.description: Name of the document where the need is defined (None if external).

doctype.description: The markup type of the content, denoted by the suffix of the source file, e.g. '.rst'.

external_css.description: CSS class name, added to the external reference.

external_url.description: URL of the need, if it is an external need.

has_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list.

has_forbidden_dead_links.description: True if any links reference need ids that are not found in the need list, and the link type does not allow dead links.

is_external.description: If true, no node is created and need is referencing external url.

is_import.description: If true, the need was derived from an import.

is_modified.description: Whether the need was modified by needextend.

jinja_content.description: Whether the content was pre-processed by jinja.

layout.description: Key of the layout, which is used to render the need.

lineno.description: Line number where the need is defined (None if external).

parts.description: Mapping of parts, a.k.a. sub-needs, IDs to data that overrides the need's data

post_template.description: The template key, if the post_content was created from a jinja template.

pre_template.description: The template key, if the pre_content was created from a jinja template.

reason.description: why it was decided this way

signature.description: Derived from a docutils desc_name node.

style.description: Comma-separated list of CSS classes (all appended by `needs_style_`).

template.description: The template key, if the content was created from a jinja template.

to.description: who has to answer a question
